text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on January 7 in history.
1502 - Pope Gregory XIII, noted for his reform of the calendar system, born.
1536 - Catherine of Aragon, first wife of King Henry VIII of England, died.
1558 - French forces captured Calais from England.
1610 - Galileo Galilei, Italian mathematician and astronomer (1564-1642), discovered Jupiter's four satellites -- Io, Europa, Gannymede and Callisto.
1785 - Dr John Jeffries and Jean Pierre Blanchard made the first crossing of the English Channel in a hot-air balloon.
1789 - The first U.S. national election took place; George Washington eventually became president.
1800 - Millard Fillmore, 13th U.S. president, born.
1844 - Marie-Bernard Soubirous, Saint Bernadette of Lourdes, born; she claimed to have seen visions of the Virgin Mary at a spring near her home and a shrine was later established there.
1845 - King Louis III, last king of Bavaria (1913-1918), born.
1867 - Carl Laemmle, U.S. film producer and founder of Universal Pictures, born.
1895 - Korea proclaimed its independence from China.
1899 - French composer and pianist Francis Poulenc born.
1904 - The shipping distress call CQD -- "seek you, danger" -- was introduced. It was replaced by SOS two years later.
1910 - Baron Alain de Rothschild, leading member of the French banking family, born.
1925 - British zoologist and writer Gerald Durrell born in India. His bestselling memoir, "My Family and Other Animals", was published in 1956; he died aged 70 in 1995.
1927 - A transatlantic telephone service between London and New York was introduced.
1937 - Princess (later Queen) Juliana of the Netherlands married Prince Bernhard.
1964 - Britain introduced internal self-government in the Bahamas.
1975 - OPEC agreed to raise the price of crude oil by 10 per cent.
1979 - Vietnamese forces, aided by Cambodian insurgents, captured Phnom Penh after a two-week invasion and overthrew the Khmer Rouge regime of Pol Pot.
1984 - French scientist Alfred Kastler died; he won the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1966 for his work which was instrumental in the development of lasers.
1989 - Emperor Hirohito of Japan died after a 63-year reign.
1994 - South Africa's Zulu-based Inkatha Freedom Party said it would not participate in the country's first all-race elections in April.
